items.title: Turn Data Into Printed Matter
items.subtitle: Make Books with Open Source Tools
items.description:
For not terribly complicated reasons — more curiosity really — I wondered if I could transform my week notes from OMATA into a book.

My rough goal was to feel like I was not going to lose track of my diaristic reflections from that 8+ year adventure.

While the data may possibly remain “somewhere” — it certainly was not on my bookshelf, and even if I contrived to shove it into some kind of digital archive or website, somehow that seemed insufficiently tangible, and possibly would disappear through the various shittification mechanisms that seem to plague so much of the web these days.

Thus I spent a wonderfully bewildering, engrossing and occasionally frustrating amount of time (I suppose I could check the commit log, but I'm afraid) building a set of tools that can basically transform most things into books. It's all open source, and available on GitHub if you want to check it out, fork it, or contribute. It mostly works just fine, although it was initially tuned to turn a Slack channel into a book, and then I realized well, wait a minute..what about everything else? Like..my Instagram feed? As a book?
